headline: Ministry of Culture Observed Partition Horrors Remembrance Day Across Delhi, Amritsar and Kolkata
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Ministry of Culture Observed Partition Horrors Remembrance Day Across Delhi, Amritsar and Kolkata

States and Union Territories also hold observance across the country

Programmes remembered the victims of Partition and honoured the resilience of those affected

15 AUG 2026 10:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Culture, Government of India, observed Partition Horrors Remembrance Day on 14 August 2026 with a series of commemorative programmes held across Delhi, Amritsar and Kolkata, remembering the immense human suffering, displacement and loss associated with the Partition of India. The observances sought to preserve the memories of those who endured the trauma of Partition, honour their courage and resilience, and remind future generations of the importance of unity, social harmony and human dignity.

Delhi: Main Observance at Central Park, Connaught Place

In New Delhi, the Ministry of Culture organised the main observance at Central Park, Connaught Place, which was graced by Shri Vivek Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in the august presence of Dr. Sachidanand Joshi, Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA); Shri Manoj Kumar Dwivedi, Chairperson & Member, NDMC; Shri K. Mahesh, Secretary, Art, Culture & Languages Department, Government of NCT of Delhi; and Prof. Ravi Prakash Tekchandani, Department of Indian Languages & Literary Studies, University of Delhi. The programme featured a solemn remembrance ceremony and a Partition Horrors Exhibition, showcasing archival material, photographs, maps and personal narratives that brought alive the human stories and experiences of Partition.

On the morning of 14th August 2026, the exhibition was inaugurated by Shri Ashish Sood, Hon’ble Minister for Home, Power, Urban Development, Education, Higher Education, Training & Technical Education, Government of NCT of Delhi, and was opened to citizens and students, with school children visiting the exhibition between 11 AM and 3 PM. The initiative provided young visitors an opportunity to engage with the history of Partition and understand the experiences of those who endured displacement, separation and loss.

The programme also featured the official screening/release of a short documentary highlighting the history, cultural heritage and contribution of displaced and Partition-affected communities. A compilation of poems titled “देहरी भई विदेश” (कविता संग्रह), compiled by Dr. Sachidanand Joshi, Member Secretary, IGNCA, and Prof. Ravi Prakash Tekchandani, Department of Indian Languages & Literary Studies, University of Delhi, was also introduced and formally released during the programme. The compilation brings together poetic reflections on the memories, experiences and human dimensions of Partition. The programme further featured an address by the Hon’ble Chief Minister, Government of NCT of Delhi, followed by the singing of the National Song “Vande Mataram”.

Following the observance, a Silent March was organised in and around the Central Park, Connaught Place as a solemn tribute to those who lost their lives, were displaced from their homes or endured the hardships of Partition. The Ministry also facilitated wider outreach of the Partition Horrors Exhibition, with exhibition material being made available for display at railway stations and other public spaces, enabling travellers and citizens to engage with this important chapter of India's history. Public service announcements were also proposed to reinforce the message that the tragedies of the past must never be repeated.

Amritsar: Remembering the Punjab Experience

Partition Horrors Remembrance Day was observed at Guru Nanak Dev University (GNDU), Amritsar, yesterday, commemorating the millions of lives affected by the Partition of India and remembering the immense suffering, displacement and sacrifices endured by people during one of the most tragic chapters in the history of the nation.

The programme was graced by Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Hon’ble Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, as the Chief Guest. The event was also attended by Dr. Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha; Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha; and Shri Tarun Chugh, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha.

As part of the observance, a Silent March was organised, with hundreds of students, and local citizens participating. The march served as a solemn tribute to those who lost their lives, homes and livelihoods during the Partition, while underscoring the importance of remembering history and preserving the stories of those who lived through it.

The programme also featured a theatrical presentation of the acclaimed play “Jis Lahore Nai Dekhya O Jamyai Nai”, based on the Partition and its human impact. The play was performed by the Harpal Tiwana Centre for Performing Arts, bringing alive the pain, resilience and shared humanity of people caught amid the upheaval of Partition.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat emphasised the importance of remembering the horrors of Partition and preserving the memories and experiences of those who suffered during the period. He highlighted that remembrance is not merely about recalling the past, but also about drawing lessons from history and strengthening the values of unity, harmony and peace.

A special exhibition on the Partition was also organised as part of the observance. The exhibition showcased photographs, archival material, documents and narratives reflecting the experiences and hardships of people during Partition. It witnessed enthusiastic participation from a large number of school students and university students, who engaged with the exhibits and gained a deeper understanding of this significant chapter in India’s history.

The participation of hundreds of students and citizens reflected a strong sense of collective remembrance and reaffirmed the importance of engaging the younger generation with the historical experiences of Partition.

The observance at GNDU was a solemn reminder of the human cost of Partition and a tribute to the courage and resilience of those who endured its profound hardships. It also reinforced the message that remembering history is essential to building a more united, peaceful and inclusive future.

Kolkata: Remembering the Bengal Experience

In Kolkata, Partition Horrors Remembrance Day was observed at the Newtown Convention Centre in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal through a two-day programme on 13 and 14 August 2026.

A special exhibition titled “The Partition of India: Memory, Loss and Resilience” was organised in Kolkata on 13 August 2026 in observance of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. The exhibition was inaugurated by Shri Dipak Barman, Hon’ble Minister of Education, Government of West Bengal, and was visited by more than 1,000 students, providing the younger generation an opportunity to engage directly with archival material and the lived experiences of Partition. The exhibition continued as part of the two-day observance and focused on the distinctive experience of Bengal during Partition, including displacement, migration and rehabilitation, and the profound social, cultural and economic impact on the region.

The 14 August programme was attended by Shri R. N. Ravi, Hon’ble Governor of West Bengal as the Chief Guest in august presence of Shri Swapan Dasgupta, Hon’ble Minister (in-charge), Finance Department, Government of West Bengal; Smt. Purnima Chakraborty, Hon’ble Minister of State, Department of Information and Cultural Affairs & Tourism, Government of West Bengal; Dr. Saumitra Mohan, Secretary, I&CA Department, Government of West Bengal; and Shri K.S. Murali, Director General, NCSM, Ministry of Culture, Government of India, along with senior government officials, distinguished scholars, artists, representatives of civil society, students and other dignitaries.

The programme sought to sensitise the younger generation to the suffering caused by Partition without inheriting hatred and to draw from history a renewed commitment to peace, social harmony, mutual respect and human dignity. Four films on Partition were also screened as part of the programme.

The observance also highlighted the experience of people whose homes, families and communities were disrupted by Partition. The communal violence in Calcutta in 1946 and the subsequent turmoil in Bengal were recalled as part of the wider historical context, while emphasising courage, dialogue and reconciliation during a period of fear and mistrust.

The programme also highlighted the history of Partition as a history of resilience, renewal and nation-building. Refugees who arrived with limited possessions and uncertain futures went on to become teachers, entrepreneurs, professionals, artists, workers, public servants and institution-builders, making significant contributions to the social, economic and cultural life of West Bengal.

The contribution of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee during the critical years preceding Partition and his opposition to the proposal for an undivided Bengal to be included in Pakistan, as well as his advocacy for the creation of a separate province to safeguard the future and interests of Bengali Hindus, was also highlighted in the programme.

The programme concluded with a candlelight march, paying tribute to the victims and survivors of Partition and acknowledging the immense contribution of Partition-affected families to the making of modern West Bengal and India. Partition Horrors Remembrance Day was also observed across all district headquarters in West Bengal.

IGNCA Programmes Across the Country

As part of the nationwide observance of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day 2026, the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, organised a series of academic, cultural and public outreach programmes at its Regional Centres, providing platforms for documenting memories, engaging younger generations and reflecting on the human experiences of Partition.

Jammu & Kashmir: Memories of Survivors and Panel Discussion

IGNCA Regional Centre, Jammu & Kashmir, in collaboration with the District Administration, Rajouri and Baba Ghulam Shah Badshah University, Rajouri, organised “Memories of Survivors: Panel Discussion on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day”, focusing on documenting and preserving the memories, struggles and experiences of people displaced from Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir during 1947 and 1965. Shri Ramesh Kumar, IAS, Divisional Commissioner, Jammu, was the Chief Guest, while Smt. Devyani Singh Rana, Hon’ble MLA, Nagrota; Prof. Javed Iqbal, Vice-Chancellor, Baba Ghulam Shah Badshah University; and Shri Abhishek Sharma, IAS, Deputy Commissioner, Rajouri, were present. A special highlight was the testimony of 99-year-old Shri Bakshi Yog Raj Chhibber, who shared his first-hand memories of Partition, along with accounts of other displaced families. An exhibition on Partition and a documentary produced by the District Administration, Rajouri, were also presented. Historians, academicians, researchers, media representatives and students from universities and institutions across the Jammu region participated in the programme.

Bengaluru: Student Procession and Documentary Screening

IGNCA Regional Centre, Bengaluru, organised a procession on 14 August 2026 at Vijaya Bharathi Vidyalaya, with the participation of more than 500 students, who carried the Tricolour in remembrance of the victims and hardships of Partition and reaffirmed the values of unity, peace and national solidarity. The observance began with a documentary screening portraying the experiences and memories of those affected by Partition, followed by an insightful talk by Dr. G. B. Harisha on the human dimensions and significance of remembering Partition. The programme was graced by Shri D. Mahendra, Regional Director, IGNCA Regional Centre, Bengaluru, and Prof. P. V. Krishna Bhatta, eminent academician and educationalist.

Ranchi: Padayatra, Exhibition, Special Lecture and Tribal & Regional Language Poets’ Gathering

IGNCA Regional Centre, Ranchi, in collaboration with Ranchi University, organised a special programme comprising a Padayatra, Partition Exhibition, Special Lecture and the Third Tribal and Regional Language Poets’ Gathering on the theme “Displacement”. Prof. Saroj Sharma, Vice-Chancellor, Ranchi University, was the Chief Guest, while Padma Shri Balbir Dutt, senior journalist and author, delivered the special lecture and Swami Bhaveshananda, Secretary, Ramakrishna Mission Ashram, Ranchi, was the Distinguished Guest. The programme brought together historical reflection, personal memories, visual documentation and poetry in tribal and regional languages, exploring displacement, memory, identity, loss and resilience. The exhibition presented visual and documentary material relating to Partition, while poets from several tribal and regional language traditions highlighted the role of indigenous languages in preserving collective memory and lived experiences.

Besides these programmes, Partition Horrors Remembrance Day was also observed across States and Union Territories on 14 August 2026 reaffirming the shared national commitment to remembering the victims and preserving the lessons of Partition.

Remembering so that history is never repeated

Partition resulted in one of the largest episodes of forced migration in modern history, with millions of people displaced across the newly created borders. The tragedy affected communities across Punjab, Bengal, Delhi and several other regions, leaving a lasting imprint on generations of families.

Through its programmes in Delhi, Amritsar and Kolkata, the Ministry of Culture sought to ensure that these memories remained part of India's collective consciousness. The observances went beyond remembering the tragedy to drawing lessons from it—rejecting hatred and division, strengthening social harmony, and reaffirming the values of unity and human dignity.

The programmes provided citizens, particularly younger generations, an opportunity to engage with the history of Partition and understand the experiences of those who lived through one of the most traumatic chapters in India's history. The observance of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day 2026 thus served as a solemn tribute to those who suffered, an acknowledgement of the resilience of survivors, and a reminder that the lessons of history must continue to guide future generations.

headline: Suryapath Tiranga: India’s Tricolour Completes a Historic Global Relay Across Continents, Following the Path of the Rising Sun
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Suryapath Tiranga: India’s Tricolour Completes a Historic Global Relay Across Continents, Following the Path of the Rising Sun

From Fiji at 1:30 AM to San Francisco at 8:30 PM IST, the Tiranga travels across 54 missions and posts in a unique global relay on Independence Day

Mass singing of Vande Mataram and Jana Gana Mana resonate across celebrations at missions and posts across the world

15 AUG 2026 10:03PM by PIB Delhi

In a spectacular global celebration of India’s Independence Day, the Suryapath Tiranga, a special initiative under Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 has carried the spirit of the National Flag across the world, following the path of the rising sun from Fiji at 1:30 AM IST to San Francisco at 8:30 PM IST. The unique global relay has connected 54 missions and posts across countries and continents, turning the movement of the sun into a symbolic journey of the Tiranga across the globe.

Beginning in Suva, Fiji at 1:30 AM IST, the Tiranga moved successively through New Zealand, Australia, Japan, the Republic of Korea, China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka and the Maldives. The relay then continued westward through Central and West Asia, including Uzbekistan, Oman, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, before reaching Africa and Europe. Each successive flag-hoisting marked another chapter in the unfolding global celebration of India’s Independence Day.

The journey subsequently crossed Ethiopia, Russia, Kenya, Israel, Egypt and South Africa, before moving across Europe through Latvia, Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, France, the United Kingdom, Spain, Morocco and Iceland. The Tiranga then crossed the Atlantic, reaching the Americas through Brazil, Suriname, Guyana, Argentina, Trinidad & Tobago, the Dominican Republic, the United States, Colombia, Canada, Jamaica, Peru and Mexico, before the relay's scheduled final stop at San Francisco at 8:30 PM IST.

The Suryapath Tiranga has thus created a remarkable chain of flag-hoisting ceremonies spanning more than 19 hours and 54 missions/posts, geographically linking the Pacific, Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas. From the first light of the day in the Pacific to the evening skies of North America, the Tiranga has symbolically travelled with the sun, carrying a message of national pride, unity and India's global presence.

A defining feature of the celebrations has been the collective cultural expression accompanying the hoisting of the National Flag. Mass singing of India’s National Song, Vande Mataram, and the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana, has formed an integral part of the programmes at missions and posts, bringing together members of the Indian diaspora, officials and friends of India in a shared expression of patriotism. The initiative also gives special resonance to 150 years of India’s National Song Vande Mataram, being commemorated this year.

The global relay is part of Har Ghar Tiranga 2026, which is being celebrated with unprecedented participation across India and abroad. The initiative seeks to take the Tiranga beyond geographical boundaries and make it a shared symbol of pride for Indians wherever they may be. Through Suryapath Tiranga, the National Flag has become the thread connecting celebrations across different time zones—one Tiranga, one journey, a world united in the spirit of India.

The initiative also reflects the growing participation of the Indian diaspora and India's missions and posts abroad in Har Ghar Tiranga. From the Pacific Islands to Europe, Africa and the Americas, the hoisting of the Tiranga and collective singing of Vande Mataram and Jana Gana Mana have created a shared moment of celebration, demonstrating the enduring emotional bond between India and its global community.

Suryapath Tiranga stands as a visual and symbolic expression of India's timeless connection with its people across the world: as the sun moves from east to west, the Tiranga follows its path—carrying India's pride, heritage and spirit across continents.

The 1st edition of SURYAPATH TIRANGA GLOBAL RELAY is now over.

headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, in his address from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day says, building a secure Bharat is the responsibility of all of us
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, in his address from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day says, building a secure Bharat is the responsibility of all of us

The armed Naxalites have been defeated, but the Naxal mindset remains

We must identify this Naxal mindset, isolate such elements and connect the country's young generation with the mainstream path of building a developed nation

15 AUG 2026 9:58PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, in his address from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day said building a secure Bharat is the responsibility of all of us. He said that the armed Naxalites have been defeated, but the Naxal mindset remains. Prime Minister said we must identify this Naxal mindset, isolate such elements and connect the country's young generation with the mainstream path of building a developed nation.

In his address, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi said that Naxalism and Maoism have destroyed the future of millions of young people. For four long decades, Naxalism held large parts of the country and a vast section of its population in its grip, keeping them under the threat of the gun. It tore the Constitution to shreds, and in the effort to protect ordinary citizens of the country, more than 3,500 of our police and security personnel made the supreme sacrifice.

Prime Minister said today, I am pleased that Naxalite-Maoist violence is perhaps no longer even capable of taking its final breath. In places where Naxalites once fired their guns, where the soil was once stained with blood, today, in those very Naxal-affected regions, the Tricolour of development, trust and endeavour is flying high because these areas are becoming Naxal-free.

Prime Minister said the armed Naxalites have been defeated, but the Naxal mindset remains. These forces are looking for opportunities. They are searching for paths of violence and anarchy, and are employing various tactics to drag society onto the wrong path.

Prime Minister said we must identify this Naxal mindset. We must isolate such elements and connect the country's young generation with the mainstream path of building a developed nation.

Prime Minister said building a secure Bharat is the responsibility of all of us. Whether the challenge comes from within our borders or from across the frontier, Bharat is prepared for every eventuality. The nature of warfare is changing today. There is no longer any guarantee that a war will take place only on the battlefield or along the border.

Prime Minister said today, I am announcing from the Red Fort that in the days ahead, we will build a vibrant civil defence network. We will equip our citizens and civil defence personnel with modern systems and technologies and familiarise them with contemporary methods of preparedness.

summaryText:
### OVERVIEW  
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addressed the nation from the Red Fort on Independence Day 2026, emphasizing national security and the legacy of Naxalism. He acknowledged the defeat of armed Naxalite-Maoist violence but highlighted the persistence of the "Naxal mindset," urging its identification, isolation, and redirection of the youth toward development.  

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS  
- **Eighty years of Independence Day** were marked by Modi's address from the Red Fort ramparts.  
- The armed Naxalite-Maoist insurgency, which terrorized regions for over **four decades**, is declared to be in its final stages, with violence no longer deemed viable.  
- Acknowledgment of **approximately 3,500** security personnel who sacrificed their lives combating Naxal violence.  
- Emphasis on detecting and neutralizing residual Naxalite ideologies, particularly targeting youth recruitment.  
- Announcement of a **civil defence network** strategy to prepare citizens and personnel using **modern technologies** and updated preparedness frameworks.  
- Reiteration that national security is a collective responsibility, encompassing both internal and external threats.

headline: Union Minister Shri Jual Oram and Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, Jointly Release National Framework and Operational Guidelines for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs
fullText:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs

Union Minister Shri Jual Oram and Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, Jointly Release National Framework and Operational Guidelines for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs

Twin publications, translate a nationwide consultative exercise covering 217 ITDAs/ITDPs across 19 States/UTs into an actionable reform roadmap for last-mile tribal development delivery

15 AUG 2026 9:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister for Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, and Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, today jointly released two important publications of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs — the “National Framework for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs” and the “Operational Guidelines for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs.” The two documents mark the culmination of a comprehensive, consultative and evidence-based national exercise aimed at strengthening Integrated Tribal Development Agencies and Projects (ITDAs/ITDPs), the principal field-level institutions driving tribal development across the country.

The publications were released in the presence of Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Tribal Affairs, Shri Manish Thakur, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and other senior officers of the Ministry.

Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted that ITDAs/ITDPs have historically served as a critical bridge between government programmes and tribal communities, and that their role has grown even more significant with the scale of interventions under the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) and PM-JANMAN.

Dr. Balasubramaniam noted that the principles of ranking, real-time data-driven monitoring and convergence that delivered saturation of outcomes in under-developed districts and blocks now stand embedded in the ITDA/ITDP reform architecture. He observed that evidence-based administrative attention can transform lagging regions, these publications seek to replicate that model within the tribal development ecosystem, using ITDAs as the delivery vehicle for saturation of entitlements at the last mile.

The exercise was undertaken under the overall guidance and vision of Secretary, Tribal Affairs, Smt. Ranjana Chopra, whose emphasis on evidence-based, field-driven institutional reform shaped the design of the entire consultative process. Smt. Chopra’s consistent direction to move beyond a one-size-fits-all approach and build context-specific, accountable

field institutions provided the strategic anchor for the Ministry’s roadmap for strengthening ITDAs and ITDPs across the country.

The Ministry had initiated this exercise in April 2026, covering 214 ITDAs/ITDPs across 17 States/UTs, through a standardised assessment involving Project Officers, State Tribal Welfare Departments and Tribal Research Institutes. Designed as a bottom-up, consultative exercise rather than a desk-based study, it included State-level workshops, field visits and direct consultations, allowing ground-level challenges and successful practices to shape the national roadmap. The exercise culminated in the Evidence-Weighted ITDA Diagnostic Scoring Framework, assessing institutions across 15 parameters spanning five institutional domains.

To operationalize this exercise on the ground, structured consultative workshops were conducted across States/UTs in April and May 2026, led by Dr. Varnali Deka, Director, DAJGUA Division and Shri Jafar Malik, Deputy Secretary, EMRS. The officers engaged directly with all ITDA/ITDP Project Officers and State Tribal Research Institutes to understand institutional status, collate ground-level data, followed by detailed validation exercise to ensure that the diagnostic exercise remained firmly rooted in field realities. These findings were then analyzed to create a national framework, roadmap and a set of operational guidelines.

This exercise reached a major milestone on 3rd June 2026, when the Ministry convened the National Conclave on Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, graced by the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu.

The National Framework provides the assessment methodology and strategic direction, while the Operational Guidelines translate these recommendations into practical measures relating to institutional restructuring, convergence, evidence-based planning, digital governance, outcome-based monitoring and capacity building. For the first time, a common institutional assessment methodology has been made available to States, enabling each ITDA to identify its gaps and prepare a Performance Improvement Roadmap suited to its own context.

Shri Jual Oram said the objective is not merely to rank institutions but to build a culture of continuous institutional improvement, and urged States to undertake State-level reviews with all ITDA/ITDP Project Officers, prepare institution-specific action plans and establish quarterly monitoring of institutional performance, on the lines of the district and block-level monitoring cadence followed under ADP and ABP.

The Minister recommended strengthening the ITDA/ITDP ecosystem through a more efficient fund-flow mechanism, including exploring direct transfer of funds to ITDAs; augmenting technical manpower for better project execution; and institutionalizing regular Governing Council meetings with active participation of PRI representatives and senior State leadership to improve convergence, accountability and implementation.

Both dignitaries congratulated the States, Project Officers, Tribal Research Institutes and Ministry officials whose field experience shaped the two publications.

(Release ID: 2300052)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has released two publications, a National Framework and Operational Guidelines, to strengthen Integrated Tribal Development Agencies and Projects (ITDAs/ITDPs) across the country. The guidelines aim to improve institutional performance, convergence, evidence-based planning, and monitoring in tribal development delivery.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
* The two publications, "National Framework for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs" and "Operational Guidelines for Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs," mark the culmination of a nationwide consultative exercise covering 217 ITDAs/ITDPs across 19 States/UTs.
* The exercise was initiated in April 2026 and involved a standardized assessment, State-level workshops, field visits, and direct consultations to understand ground-level challenges and successful practices.
* The Evidence-Weighted ITDA Diagnostic Scoring Framework assessed institutions across 15 parameters spanning five institutional domains.
* The Operational Guidelines translate recommendations into practical measures, including institutional restructuring, convergence, evidence-based planning, digital governance, outcome-based monitoring, and capacity building.
* For the first time, a common institutional assessment methodology is available to States, enabling each ITDA to identify gaps and prepare a Performance Improvement Roadmap suited to its context.
* The Minister recommended strengthening the ITDA/ITDP ecosystem through a more efficient fund-flow mechanism, augmenting technical manpower, and institutionalizing regular Governing Council meetings.
* The exercise reached a major milestone on June 3, 2026, with the National Conclave on Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, graced by the Hon'ble President of India.

headline: DAE-Nurtured Yuva Shakti Honoured at the Red Fort as International Olympiad Achievers 2026 Join the 80th Independence Day Celebrations as Special Guests
fullText:
Department of Atomic Energy

DAE-Nurtured Yuva Shakti Honoured at the Red Fort as International Olympiad Achievers 2026 Join the 80th Independence Day Celebrations as Special Guests

As the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi hoists the National Flag and addresses the nation, young Indian achievers from the International Science and Mathematical Olympiads 2026 witness the 80th Independence Day Ceremony at the Red Fort in New Delhi as Special Guests

The recognition celebrates India’s Yuva Shakti, a key force in the nation’s journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047, during the year marking 150 years of Vande Mataram

The achievements reflect the strength of India's National Olympiad Programme, spearheaded by the Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (HBCSE), a National Centre of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), an aided institution under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)

The Special Guests participated in a series of engagements in New Delhi, including interactions with Dr. Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Minister of State, PMO, and Dr. Ajit Kumar Mohanty, Secretary to Government of India, Department of Atomic Energy & Chairman, Atomic Energy Commission.

15 AUG 2026 9:00PM by PIB Delhi

India’s Yuva Shakti took centre stage at the historic Red Fort as young Indian medallists from the International Science and Mathematical Olympiads 2026 joined the nation’s Independence Day celebrations as Special Guests of the Government of India. The young achievers witnessed Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji hoist the Indian Tricolour and address the nation from the ramparts of the iconic Red Fort in New Delhi on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day.

The recognition of these young achievers was a celebration of the immense potential of India’s youth and their contribution to the nation’s journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047. Coming in a year commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram, the presence of the Olympiad achievers at the national ceremony was a powerful affirmation of the Hon. Prime Minister’s emphasis on harnessing the energy, talent and aspirations of India’s Yuva Shakti in building a developed and self-reliant nation.

The honour comes in the wake of an exceptional year for India at the International Olympiads. Across Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Mathematics, Indian students won 12 Gold and 7 Silver Medals in 2026. The distinction bestowed on the students at the Red Fort is also a recognition of the sustained national effort to identify and nurture exceptional scientific and mathematical talent from a young age.

At the heart of this national endeavour is HBCSE, a National Centre of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), an aided institution under the Department of Atomic Energy. As the national nodal centre for the Science and Mathematical Olympiad Programmes, HBCSE follows a rigorous multi-stage process of selection, orientation, training and mentoring. The Department of Atomic Energy has been a pillar of strength behind this enduring national effort. Through its support to TIFR and HBCSE, the Department of Atomic Energy has helped build an ecosystem that brings together scientists, teachers, academic institutions and subject experts from across the country in a shared mission of nurturing scientific talent. This institutional support extends beyond the conduct of competitions to sustained training, mentoring and participation at the international level.

The Special Guests’ visit to New Delhi extended beyond the Independence Day ceremony. The young achievers arrived in the capital and interacted Dr. Ajit Kumar Mohnaty, Secretary, Department of Atomic Energy & Chairman, Atomic Energy Commission. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Mohanty said, “It is a matter of immense pride that our young Olympiad achievers are being honoured as Special Guests at the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort. Their presence at this iconic national occasion is a fitting recognition of India's Yuva Shakti and the spirit of curiosity, perseverance and excellence that they represent. The outstanding performance of our students at the International Olympiads is also a reflection of the sustained national effort to identify and nurture scientific and mathematical talent. The Department of Atomic Energy is privileged to contribute to this endeavour through its support to TIFR and HBCSE, and remains committed to strengthening this ecosystem so that India's young minds have every opportunity to excel, innovate and contribute to the making of a Viksit Bharat@2047.”

The students interacted with Dr. Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Minister of State in PMO Department of Atomic Energy and visited sites of national significance, including the National War Memorial and the Pradhan Mantri Sangrahalaya.

The Department of Atomic Energy congratulates the young Olympiad achievers, their parents, teachers, mentors, team leaders, scientific observers, Olympiad Cells at HBCSE and the nationwide community of resource persons whose dedication has contributed to these remarkable accomplishments.

The presence of these young scientists and mathematicians at the Red Fort was more than an honour bestowed on a group of medal winners. It was a celebration of India’s capacity to identify excellence, nurture talent and provide its young citizens the opportunity to excel at the highest global level. As India marches towards Viksit Bharat@2047, the achievements and aspirations of these young Olympians offer an inspiring glimpse of the Yuva Shakti that will shape the nation’s future.

headline: Akademies under the Ministry of Culture Mark 80th Independence Day with Nationwide Cultural Programmes under ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ and 150 Years of Vande Mataram
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Akademies under the Ministry of Culture Mark 80th Independence Day with Nationwide Cultural Programmes under ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ and 150 Years of Vande Mataram

15 AUG 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Akademies under the Ministry of Culture celebrated the 80th Independence Day with patriotic fervour through a wide range of cultural and participatory activities under the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign. Across the country, the celebrations included Tiranga rallies and yatras, flag-hoisting ceremonies, mass singing of Vande Mataram, patriotic theatre and musical performances, art and painting workshops, wall paintings, clay modelling, traditional crafts, exhibitions and student-centric activities. These initiatives brought together students, artists, cultural practitioners and citizens, showcasing India’s rich cultural diversity and spirit of unity in diversity, while fostering patriotism, national pride and collective participation and commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram.

The National School of Drama (NSD) and its centres across the country engaged citizens and students through a range of programmes celebrating the spirit of Har Ghar Tiranga and the 80th Independence Day. NSD created awareness about the celebrations and the 150th year of Vande Mataram through its social media and other communication platforms, while sensitising citizens about the proper display of the National Flag and encouraging participation in the ‘Selfie with Tiranga’ initiative. More than 250 NSDians uploaded their selfies on the portal. NSD also conducted a mass singing of Vande Mataram at its campus and organised a rally of around 400 participants in the Mandi House area on 14 August. On 15 August, an interaction programme on patriotism for students was organised at the NSD Delhi campus.

Across its regional centres, NSD Bengaluru organised a bike rally and three plays on patriotism. The NSD TIE Centre, Tripura, conducted a procession promoting Har Ghar Tiranga, collaborated with the Lalit Kala Akademi on a Tiranga-themed wall-painting project and organised a cultural programme. The NSD Varanasi Centre organised a rally with Rang Sangeet and patriotic performances, while the NSD Sikkim Centre also conducted programmes to mark the occasion. In Srinagar, NSD’s first-year students joined Kashmiri artists at Lal Mandi on 14 August for Watan Ke Rang, Kashmir Ke Sang, featuring theatre, Kashmiri folk dances, Bhand Pather and Lal Ded Vak, opening with Vande Mataram and concluding with Jana Gana Mana.

The Sahitya Akademi participated in the nationwide celebrations through Tiranga Yatras, Tiranga Selfie activities, Tricolour illumination and decoration of its premises, and mass singing of Vande Mataram. It also observed Vibhajan Vibhishika Smriti Diwas at Hansraj College, University of Delhi, with around 200 students participating. The programme recalled the suffering, displacement and human cost associated with Partition while encouraging young people to engage with this chapter of the nation’s history and reinforcing the values of peace, harmony, mutual respect and national unity. Through these activities, the Akademi highlighted the role of literature and cultural engagement in strengthening citizens’ connection with the nation.

The Sangeet Natak Akademi presented a five-segment thematic musical programme showcasing folk and traditional musical heritage from Chhattisgarh and Bastar, Maharashtra, Goa and Madhya Pradesh. The presentation opened with Mangal Dhun and moved through community celebration rhythms of Maharashtra, the festive traditions of Goa’s Konkan coast and indigenous musical traditions of Madhya Pradesh. It culminated in a finale bringing together musicians and instruments from all four regions, conveying the message of “Unity in Diversity”. The Akademi also arranged a traditional musical welcome for dignitaries featuring Tasha, Tutari, Dhol and Shank.

The Lalit Kala Akademi celebrated Independence Day through visual arts activities, rallies, workshops and public participation programmes across its headquarters and Regional Centres. At its headquarters in New Delhi, the Akademi, in association with the Sahitya Akademi and Sangeet Natak Akademi, organised the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ programme and flag hoisting at Rabindra Bhawan on 13 August 2026. The programme was followed by a Tiranga Rally in which more than 1,500 participants, including schoolchildren, working artists, art enthusiasts and local residents, participated.

Its Regional Centres also organised a range of activities. At Agartala, a student rally and wall-painting programme were organised at Nazrul Kala Kshetra, involving students and senior artists. At Shimla, a Tricolour Rally was organised on 13 August with students of PM Shri Kendriya Vidyalaya Jakhoo Hills and Jawaharlal Nehru Fine Arts College, Shimla, along with a painting workshop at the Lalit Kala Akademi Art Gallery, Gaiety Theatre.

The Regional Centre, Ahmedabad, organised a Tiranga Rally and Clay Modelling Workshop on 15 August under the theme “Viksit Bharat 2047 – Mitti Se Bharat”, with around 15 schoolchildren participating. At Kolkata, the Regional Centre organised the Har Ghar Tiranga programme, an art workshop and a sit-and-draw programme, with more than 1,000 school students and 300 working artists, college students and art enthusiasts participating, followed by a Tiranga Rally involving more than 1,500 participants. Flag-hoisting ceremonies were also held at both campuses on 15 August, with the buildings illuminated in Tricolour lights.

The Lucknow Regional Centre organised a Children’s Painting Workshop on 12 August, followed by a Tiranga Rally on 13 August in which approximately 1,500 people participated, as well as a patriotic cultural programme. A flag-hoisting ceremony was also held at the Centre on 15 August. The Chennai Regional Centre observed Independence Day with a flag-hoisting ceremony attended by staff members, artists and art lovers.

The Kalakshetra Foundation observed the Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign 2026 across its four units through educational, artistic and participatory activities. The campaign included pledges, Tricolour illumination, flag distribution, Tricolour-themed decoration and mass singing of Vande Mataram and the National Anthem by students and staff. Students participated in rangoli, art-from-waste, clay modelling, vegetable carving and salad-making using Tricolour themes, as well as presentations on Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

The Foundation also undertook traditional craft activities including Tricolour weaving, natural dyeing, Kalamkari work and making of flags and Tricolour-themed crafts. The celebrations featured a puppet show on unsung heroes, women warriors and freedom fighters, a fancy-dress competition on national leaders and freedom fighters, and rallies and public exhibitions, bringing together students, teachers, artists, craftspeople and members of the public. The campaign culminated in the 80th Independence Day celebrations on 15 August 2026.

Through the collective efforts of the Akademies, the celebrations brought the spirit of Har Ghar Tiranga into cultural spaces across the country. From theatre and music to painting, literature, traditional crafts and community participation, the programmes provided diverse platforms for citizens, particularly young people, to connect with the values of patriotism, national pride and cultural heritage. The celebrations also commemorated 150 years of Vande Mataram while showcasing the many artistic traditions that contribute to India’s cultural identity. Through these nationwide initiatives, the Akademies reaffirmed the message of unity in diversity and a shared commitment to the nation.

headline: Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Interacts with MY Bharat-NSS Volunteers at Independence Day Celebrations
fullText:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Interacts with MY Bharat-NSS Volunteers at Independence Day Celebrations

Energy, Commitment and Innovative Ideas of Youth are Essential for Achieving the Vision of Viksit Bharat : Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya

15 AUG 2026 7:45PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya interacted with MY Bharat-NSS volunteers during the Independence Day celebrations at Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, New Delhi, recognising the contribution and active participation of young volunteers in the national celebrations.

MY Bharat-NSS volunteers participated as special guests at the Independence Day programme, providing them an opportunity to witness the celebrations and engage with the Union Minister. Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya interacted with the volunteers and encouraged their continued participation in nation-building and civic engagement.

Addressing the volunteers, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya appreciated their contribution towards social service and encouraged them to actively participate in initiatives aimed at building a Viksit Bharat. He emphasised that the energy, commitment and innovative ideas of young people are essential for achieving the vision of a developed and self-reliant India.

The programme also provided a platform for volunteers to share their experiences, ideas and aspirations. The interaction reaffirmed the commitment of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to provide meaningful opportunities for youth participation and leadership in nation-building.

Earlier in the morning as part of the Independence Day celebrations, MY Bharat-NSS volunteers and students from eight schools and educational institutions across Delhi came together to create a large-scale human formation representing ‘Vande Mataram’. Around 500 students participated in the formation, showcasing patriotism, national unity and collective participation.

headline: Union Home Minister & Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to lay the foundation stone of new dairy plant at Alwar Saras Dairy Complex tomorrow
fullText:
Ministry of Cooperation

Union Home Minister & Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to lay the foundation stone of new dairy plant at Alwar Saras Dairy Complex tomorrow

E-inauguration of Dairy Processing Plants and Cattle Feed Plants of various Milk Unions to be held

E-foundation stone laying and e-inauguration of diverse development works worth ₹6,262 crore across 17 districts

Important initiative towards empowering cooperative institutions and farmers in line with the mantra of "Sahkar se Samriddhi"

15 AUG 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of "Sahkar se Samriddhi," Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will lay the foundation stone of a new dairy plant at the Alwar Saras Dairy Complex, Vijay Nagar Ground, Alwar, Rajasthan, on 16th August 2026. On this occasion, Shri Amit Shah will also e-inaugurate the Dairy Processing Plants and Cattle Feed Plants of various milk unions.

During the programme, Hon'ble Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will announce the formation of new Central Cooperative Banks and will remotely transfer funds to beneficiaries of various welfare schemes through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). These beneficiaries will include those covered under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana.

At the event, the e-foundation stone laying and e-inauguration of various development works worth ₹6,262 crore across 17 districts of Rajasthan. Additionally, appointment letters will be distributed to 10548 newly appointed personnel under the Rozgar Utsav.

The foundation stone laying of the new dairy plant at Alwar Saras Dairy Complex and the e-inauguration of various dairy processing and cattle feed plants will be an important step towards strengthening the processing and production capacity of the dairy cooperative sector in the state. This will boost modern dairy infrastructure, create better opportunities for milk producers, and contribute to further strengthening the rural economy through cooperation.

This initiative, in line with the mantra of "Sahkar se Samriddhi" given by Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, will further reinforce the Government's commitment to making cooperative institutions modern, efficient and self-reliant, and to economically empowering farmers and milk producers through cooperation.

(Release ID: 2299953)

headline: Libraries under the Ministry of Culture, Asiatic Society Kolkata and The Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (MAKAIS) Kolkata celebrate 80th Independence Day 2026 with patriotic zeal
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Libraries under the Ministry of Culture, Asiatic Society Kolkata and The Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (MAKAIS) Kolkata celebrate 80th Independence Day 2026 with patriotic zeal

15 AUG 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Libraries under the Ministry of Culture, Asiatic Society Kolkata and The Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (MAKAIS) Kolkata celebrated the 80th Independence Day of India by organizing a series of programmes and activities. The celebrations included flag hoisting ceremonies, singing of patriotic songs, programmes, exhibitions, lectures, book displays, Tiranga Yatra, and other activities highlighting the country's freedom struggle and the spirit of patriotism.

National Library, Kolkata organized Independence Day समारोह with the rendition of Vande Mataram, followed by the welcome of guests, inspection of the parade and flag hoisting by the Director General and the singing of the National Anthem. The Director General, National Library addressed the gathering of officers and employees of the National Library. Independence Day was celebrated with patriotic fervour through a range of activities including a Tiranga Yatra, “Selfie with Tiranga” and other programmes to encourage public participation and spread the spirit of patriotism.

Delhi Public Library on the eve of Independence Day celebrations is organizing a series of programmes from 9th to 17th August 2026 at its branches and sub-branches across Delhi, including the Chandni Chowk Library. The activities include special illumination and decoration of regional libraries, programmes on the role of youth, women and students in the Quit India Movement, Selfie Points and Tiranga Yatra, observance of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, and dignified flag hoisting ceremonies.

Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library, Patna, will organize an exhibition of books on the theme “Patriotism” from 14 to 17 August 2026. A flag hoisting ceremony was held on 15th August 2026 followed by a lecture on the “Freedom Movement” on 17 August 2026 .

The Independence Day programme at Central Reference Library, Kolkata, started with a welcome address and flag hoisting by Lt. Col. Dr. Anant Sinha, SLIO, followed by the singing of the National Anthem, full rendition of Vande Mataram by the staff members followed by distribution of sweets.

The Central Secretariat Library, New Delhi is organizing a display of books on the themes of the Freedom Movement and Independence Day at its Main Library, Shastri Bhawan and R.K. Puram Branch Library from 14th to 31st August 2026. A National Flag March was organized at Shastri Bhawan on 14 August 2026.

The Raja Rammohun Roy Library Foundation (RRRLF), Kolkata celebrates 80th Independence Day with the hoisting of the National Flag by its Director General, singing of the National Anthem and rendition of Vande Mataram by the officers and employees.

The Rampur Raza Library (RRL) organized a three-day themed exhibition, titled “Bharat Gatha: Sangharsh se Swadhinta, Swadhinta se Swabhiman, Swabhiman se Viksit Bharat”, from 13 to 15 August 2026. The celebrations will also include a patriotic selfie booth, tricolour illumination of the library building, tricolour rangoli depicting the map of India, installation of national flags, social media outreach, flag hoisting and group singing of Vande Mataram.

The Asiatic Society, Kolkata celebrates the 80th Independence Day on 15 August 2026 with a series of commemorative activities. The celebrations included the hoisting of the National Flag, rendition of Vande Mataram and the National Anthem, and laying a garland at the bust of Rishi Aurobindo. An exhibition titled “1857: The First War of Independence” inaugurated at the Heritage Building by Shri K.K. Mishra, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India. The Society also organised flag-hoisting ceremonies at Raja Rajendra Mitra Bhavan, Salt Lake and 91, Ballygunge Place, Kolkata.

MAKAIAS celebrated Independence Day in a befitting manner. On 13th and 14th August, two Seminars on Partition Horror were organized. Research fellows, Research assistants, University students with others participated. Films on Swami Vivekananda, Cellular Jail, Matonggini Hazra, Dr. Shyama Prasad Mookerjee were played. Video recording statements of eye witnesses were taken. Flag hoisting celebrations with Partition Horror exhibition organised on 15th August 2026.

Through these programmes, the Ministry of Culture institutions pay tribute to the independence struggle and reaffirm their commitment to preserving and promoting the values of freedom, unity, patriotism and national integration among the citizens. It also renews India’s commitment to building a strong, prosperous, progressive and self-reliant India and achieve the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

headline: DRI uncovers large-scale illegal use of SAFTA agreement in areca imports
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

DRI uncovers large-scale illegal use of SAFTA agreement in areca imports

Months long investigation reveals defrauding exchequer of over Rs. 2,500 crore (approx.); Rs. 75 lakh cash, 160 MT areca nuts seized (approx.); Nine arrested

Syndicates imported areca nuts into India from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries by mis-declaring country of origin as Bangladesh

Licence of Customs Broker firm responsible for clearance of most of the fraudulent imports of areca nuts suspended

16 AUG 2026 10:51AM by PIB Delhi

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), in a month-long intelligence-led operation, has dismantled a major network involved in importing South-East Asian areca nuts into India by falsely declaring them as Bangladeshi origin and fraudulently availing concessional duty benefits under the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA). The investigation has so far revealed a potential revenue loss of more than Rs. 2,500 crore. Nine persons have been arrested in connection with the case.

The import of areca nuts into India attracts a Basic Customs Duty (BCD) of 100%. However, eligible imports of areca nuts made under SAFTA agreement are fully exempt from customs duty. The areca nuts originating from Bangladesh are entitled to exemption under SAFTA if imports meet the prescribed Rules of Origin criterion.

Intelligence gathered and developed by DRI indicated that certain syndicates were fraudulently claiming the SAFTA benefits on a very large scale on imports of areca nuts. While they were importing areca nuts originating and sourced from Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and other South-East Asian countries, they were mis-declaring the country of origin of areca nuts imported into India as Bangladesh.

Thereafter, simultaneous searches were conducted at multiple premises linked to importers, Customs Brokers and IEC holders in Kolkata and Visakhapatnam. Several incriminating documents and substantial evidences establishing the South-East Asian origin of Areca nuts were recovered. DRI officers also recovered and seized around Rs. 75 lakh in cash, believed to be sale proceeds of the illegally imported goods. A live consignment of around 160 MT of areca nuts.

The investigations so far have revealed huge scale of fraudulent imports of areca nuts in which exchequer has been duped of customs duty in excess of Rs 2,500 crore in recent years. The masterminds were facilitating the import of areca nuts from South-East Asian countries into one of the EPZ in Bangladesh and thereafter routing the goods to India merely changing containers and bags and passing them off as Bangladeshi-origin areca nuts. They had fraudulently obtained SAFTA Certificates of Origin from Bangladeshi authorities. The masterminds were charging substantial commissions from Indian importers for arranging the routing, documentation, clearance and transportation of the consignments and massive collection of payments in cash... The investigation has also brought to light the use of hawala channels and dummy entities for movement and layering of the financial proceeds.

Investigation has further revealed that one Customs Broker firm was particularly responsible for clearance of most of the fraudulent imports of areca nuts identified in the case. Consequent to the ongoing investigation by DRI, the Customs Broker's licence has been suspended by the competent authority. Nine persons have been arrested so far in connection with the case.

Such illegal imports adversely impact domestic areca nut growers and legitimate trade by creating unfair price distortion, and disrupting the level playing field for legitimate businesses. Besides causing huge loss to the Government revenue, these illegal activities also undermine regulated trade practices and economic security in the border regions.

With this operation, DRI has effectively disrupted a well-organised network involved in systematic mis-declaration of country of origin, fraudulent availment of SAFTA benefits and large-scale evasion of customs revenue.

headline: India to Host BRICS Environment Working Group Meetings at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi (17-18 August 2026)
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

India to Host BRICS Environment Working Group Meetings at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi (17-18 August 2026)

BRICS Member Countries to deliberate on Shared Environmental Priorities and Strengthen Cooperation for a Resilient and Sustainable Future

16 AUG 2026 9:11AM by PIB Delhi

India is set to host the 12th BRICS Environment Ministers Meeting in New Delhi on 18.08.2026, preceded by the BRICS Senior Officers’ Meeting of the Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development on 17.08.2026. The event would be held under the overarching theme of India’s BRICS Chairship 2026 - ‘Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability’.

New Delhi to host BRICS Senior Officers’ Meeting & 12th Environment Ministers’ Meeting under the Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development, on 17-18 August 2026.@BricsIndia2026#BRICS2026 #BRICSIndia2026 #IndiaBRICSChairship… pic.twitter.com/pRwfxRgnTL

— MoEF&CC (@moefcc) August 16, 2026

The BRICS Environment Ministers’ Meeting would be presided over by Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav and would provide a platform for Ministers, Senior Officers, policymakers, and experts from the Member Countries to engage in substantive discussions, foster consensus, and strengthen environmental cooperation.

The first day would witness the Senior Officers’ Meeting, which would include an inaugural session and deliberations on the priorities of the BRICS Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development.

The second day would culminate in Ministerial-level deliberations on the outcome document and thematic discussions that underscore the collective commitment of BRICS Member Countries to environmental cooperation and sustainable development. As part of the Chairship, India has identified four priority areas for focused engagements under the BRICS Environment Working Group.

Priority I: Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles underscores environmental commitments by promoting sustainable lifestyles through mindful consumption and community practices, while fostering collaboration, sharing knowledge, leading practices and success stories to develop innovative approaches from the Member Countries.

Priority II: Afforestation, Forest Fire Management and Disaster Resilience focuses on strengthening land restoration by combining structured knowledge exchange and capacity building with advanced data collection, monitoring and addressing shared challenges through integrated, landscape-based greening approaches. This priority also emphasises on forest fire management, prevention, preparedness, early detection and rapid response.

Priority III: Circular Economy showcases effective waste management practices by developing robust Extended Producer Responsibility policy frameworks and regulatory approaches. This priority aims to exemplify the leading practices, across Member Countries to ensure equity and resource use efficiency which would lead to a pivotal policy instrument for advancing circular economy transitions.

Priority IV: Adaptation focuses on advancing cooperation on climate adaptation through people-centric and community-led adaptation built on traditional knowledge. This priority supports the deliberation on practical cooperation, structured knowledge exchange, exchange of best practices and policy-relevant outcomes built over traditional knowledge systems that strengthens climate resilience across BRICS Member Countries.

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, under its BRICS 2026 Chairship, initiated discussions and deliberations through a series of virtual meetings, technical sessions, webinars and dialogues during the period March to July 2026. Dialogue on BRICS Resource Efficiency and Circular Economy, and Aligning Carbon Markets with Adaptation Goals, besides Webinars on Initiatives Towards addressing Land Degradation, Desertification and Drought, and Integrated Approaches to Wildfire Management for Disaster Resilience were also organized. These consultations provided an important platform for building consensus and setting the context for in-person deliberations in New Delhi on 17th - 18th August 2026.

The BRICS Environment Working Group (EWG) was established in 2015 during the first BRICS Environment Ministers’ Meeting in Moscow. It was envisioned as a platform for BRICS to address fundamental environment priorities, exchange experiences, share best practices and strengthen collective action amongst BRICS Member Countries.

The Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development was established in 2024 as an effective mechanism for cooperation on climate change issues amongst BRICS member countries.

headline: From Daily-Wage Struggle to a Sustainable Grocery Business: How SJY and PM-AJAY Support Helped Ruby Devi Build a Better Future
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Daily-Wage Struggle to a Sustainable Grocery Business: How SJY and PM-AJAY Support Helped Ruby Devi Build a Better Future

16 AUG 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi

For women facing severe financial hardship, access to livelihood opportunities and timely financial support can play an important role in enabling them to support their families and build a more secure future.

Demonstrating how livelihood assistance can help a family overcome economic hardship, Ruby Devi, a 32-year-old woman belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) community, is a resident of Village and Panchayat Karanpura, Hajipur, Vaishali in Bihar.

She studied up to Class 8 and is now running a general store. Before joining the Sustainable Livelihood Scheme (SJY), Ruby worked as a daily-wage labourer, while her husband, Late Ram Krish Chaudhary, earned a livelihood by selling toddy.

In 2016, Ruby's husband became seriously ill and passed away due to lack of proper treatment. With two young children to care for, and with little support from her parental family, she was left to manage the household on her own. The family's financial condition became extremely weak, and arranging even two meals a day was difficult. Raising and educating her children became a major challenge, while the stress and hardship also affected Ruby's own health.

Ruby's circumstances began to change when she was selected during the SJY drive. Through Sangam JEEViKA Mahila Gram Sangathan, she received support to establish a grocery shop.

Before receiving the business assets, she underwent a three-day CBED training to understand how to run and manage the business. She initially received ₹10,000 as SIF support from Pragati JEEViKA Mahila Gram Sangathan. Through the purchasing committee, she subsequently received grocery shop support worth ₹20,000 and ₹27,000. She also received LGF support of ₹1,000 per month for seven months, totaling ₹7,000, to support her food expenses.

To strengthen her business skills, Ruby received refresher training three times at intervals of three months. She also received ₹17,000 assistance under the PM-AJAY scheme, which helped her further strengthen and expand her business and livelihood activities. In addition, she received ₹10,000 under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana.

Before joining SJY, Ruby earned only around ₹2,000–₹3,000 per month through daily-wage labour. Today, she earns approximately ₹15,000–₹20,000 per month through her grocery and general store business. Her total assets are presently valued at approximately ₹1,45,640. Before joining the scheme, she did not even have a bank account. With the improvement in her economic condition, she developed the habit of saving money and began by saving ₹10 every day.

The change in Ruby's livelihood has also supported the education and future of her children. Both of her children now attend government schools regularly, with one studying in Class 6 and the other in Class 4. Earlier, poverty made it difficult for her to send them to school. Today, Ruby is able to support their education and hopes that both her children will secure government jobs in the future.

Ruby has also become connected with several government welfare schemes and services, including a ration card, Ayushman card, gas connection, electricity connection, Indira Awas, toilet scheme, tap water scheme and insurance benefits. For healthcare needs, she visits nearby government hospitals. Her association with Sangam JEEViKA Gram Sangathan has also enabled her to participate actively in social and community activities.

Her transformation is not limited to her financial condition. Earlier, her family was looked down upon in the village because of her husband's traditional occupation of toddy selling, and she was often not invited to social functions or ceremonies. Today, her successful business, determination and active participation in community activities have earned her greater respect. People now respectfully address her as “Ruby Didi” and invite her to village events.

With the financial burden on her family reduced and her livelihood strengthened, Ruby now aspires to expand her grocery shop and establish a larger and more stable business enterprise. She hopes to receive further financial support and training opportunities to strengthen her livelihood and create better opportunities for her family.

Ruby Devi's journey from a daily-wage labourer struggling to provide basic necessities for her children to a confident general store owner earning ₹15,000–₹20,000 per month demonstrates how timely livelihood support, training, financial assistance and linkages with government welfare schemes can help women overcome economic hardship, achieve greater self-reliance and regain dignity and respect in their communities.

headline: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Emphasises early diagnosis, timely medical intervention and avoidance of unnecessary investigations as the basis of responsible patient care
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Emphasises early diagnosis, timely medical intervention and avoidance of unnecessary investigations as the basis of responsible patient care

Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches ‘Rheumatology Essentials’ Authored by Prof. Anand N. Malaviya and Dr. Prashant Kaushik

Dr. Jitendra Singh Advocates Three-Pronged Approach to Improve Clinical Management of Rheumatic and Musculoskeletal Diseases

Quality Medical Literature in Hindi Essential to Support Expansion of Medical Education in Indian Languages: Dr. Jitendra Singh

16 AUG 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, who is himself a Professor of Medicine, today called for greater emphasis on clinically guided medical practice, with early diagnosis, timely medical intervention and avoidance of unnecessary investigations as the the basis of responsible patient care.

Speaking at the launch of “Rheumatology Essentials: A New Frontier for Aspiring Clinicians”, Dr. Jitendra Singh said this three-pronged approach can help reduce unnecessary medication and investigations, prevent delays in diagnosis and ensure that patients reach the appropriate specialist at the right time.

The book, authored by eminent rheumatologists Prof. Anand N. Malaviya and Dr. Prashant Kaushik, was launched in the presence of senior members of the medical fraternity, including Dr. Uma Kumar, Head of Rheumatology, AIIMS, and Dr. Shankar Subramaniam. Prof. Malaviya is widely recognised for his pioneering contribution to rheumatology and clinical immunology in India, while Dr. Kaushik is Clinical Professor of Medicine and Chief of Rheumatology at Northeastern Health System, Oklahoma, USA. The book carries a foreword by Dr. Vinod K. Paul.

Describing Prof. Malaviya as a “teacher of teachers”, Dr. Jitendra Singh said his contribution went beyond teaching students to creating generations of clinicians and teachers who helped take rheumatology forward across the country. Recalling his early association with Prof Malviya, he said Rheumatology was once not widely recognised as a distinct super-specialty, but Prof. Malaviya's work at AIIMS helped establish its identity, credibility and institutional foundation in India.

The Minister said Prof. Malaviya not only founded the specialty but also institutionalised rheumatology through structured courses and training programmes, creating opportunities for young doctors and medical teachers from different parts of the country to receive specialised training. He said the growth in the number of trained rheumatologists and formal programmes in the discipline reflected the lasting contribution of Prof. Malaviya.

Referring to the clinical framework presented in “Rheumatology Essentials”, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the book provides clinicians with a simple and practical way to distinguish between inflammatory rheumatic diseases, mechanical-structural disorders and nociplastic pain syndromes. He said this approach can help physicians move beyond symptomatic treatment and identify patients who require specialist rheumatological care.

The Minister said the book's three-pronged strategy of “recognise disease early, avoid unnecessary investigation and ensure timely referral” is particularly relevant to contemporary medical practice. He said patients with musculoskeletal complaints can sometimes undergo repeated symptomatic treatment or move from one physician to another without the underlying condition being properly identified. A clinically guided approach can help prevent such delays and reduce avoidable treatment.

Calling for greater reliance on clinical judgement alongside modern diagnostic technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh said investigations should support clinical reasoning rather than replace it. He referred to the growing availability of immunological tests, MRI scans and other sophisticated investigations and said their appropriate use is important for ensuring responsible and ethical medical practice.

The Minister also spoke about the wider implications of musculoskeletal disorders, including reduced mobility and the management of common comorbidities such as diabetes. He said prolonged or inappropriate use of painkillers can also affect overall health, making accurate diagnosis and appropriate referral important components of patient safety.

Welcoming the book's information on DM, DNB and fellowship programmes in rheumatology across India, Dr. Jitendra Singh said it would help students and young doctors explore specialised training opportunities in the field. He also spoke about the importance of creating quality scientific and medical literature in Hindi and other Indian languages, saying language accessibility must be supported by adequate professional literature so that students are not disadvantaged by the medium of instruction.

According to the book's introductory synopsis, Rheumatology Essentials is designed for undergraduate and postgraduate medical students, primary-care physicians, general physicians and frontline emergency-room physicians. It provides a practical framework for diagnosing and triaging rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases and seeks to enable clinicians to distinguish conditions requiring specialist rheumatological care from mechanical-structural and biopsychosocial pain conditions.

Congratulating Prof. Malaviya and Dr. Kaushik on the launch, Dr. Singh said that after dedicating his professional life to rheumatology, Prof. Malaviya had chosen through the book to carry the legacy of rheumatology to future generations. He expressed the hope that the book would reach a wide range of clinicians and aspiring specialists and contribute to more ethical, informed and patient-centred medical practice.
